first_commit_message:
Add prepare-release skill for cutting the dev-side release PR (#794)

# Summary

Adds a `prepare-release` skill at
`.claude/skills/prepare-release/SKILL.md` for the maintainer-side first
step of the release process (`docs/developer.md` § "New releases", step
2): branch off dev, consolidate the accumulated `-dev` CHANGELOG
bullets, decide the right bump level per `docs/versioning.md`, rewrite
the bullets as a polished release note mirroring the grouped v3.2.1.0 /
v3.2.1.3 structure, drop the `-dev` suffix, open a
`release/<handle>/<version>` PR into dev.

# Why this exists alongside the `version-bump` agent

The existing `version-bump` agent (`.claude/agents/version-bump.md`) is
good at mid-stream PR-level bumps: a single PR justifies a higher bump
than the current `-dev`, the agent reads the diff and updates two files.
That doesn't cover the release-cut workflow, which has two
release-specific concerns:

1. **Bump classification across the *entire* accumulated `-dev`
history.** The release-level bump is the max of every `-dev` bullet's
classification. The skill walks through each bullet and the
Major/Schema/Results/Point criteria, and explicitly escalates ambiguous
cases — under-classifying a Schema or Results bump breaks downstream
compatibility commitments.

2. **CHANGELOG rewriting.** Raw `-dev` bullets accrete in PR-author
voice with implementation detail and inconsistent grouping; release
notes are user-facing outcomes grouped under `## New workflow outputs` /
`## Cleanup and best practice` / `## Bugfixes` / etc. The skill names
the "verbatim copy" path as an anti-pattern and walks through the
rewrite explicitly, with v3.2.1.0 and v3.2.1.3 as concrete exemplars.

The skill is the heavier-weight release-specific counterpart;
`version-bump` remains the right tool for mid-stream bumps.

# Scope boundaries

- The skill cuts the **dev-side release PR only.** The subsequent dev →
main release PR is a separate maintainer step (`docs/developer.md` step
3.1) and isn't automated here.
- The skill won't trigger an index rebuild. Most releases don't need a
new index; when they do, the maintainer takes the additional steps in
`docs/developer.md` step 2.3 (update `index-min-pipeline-version` /
`pipeline-min-index-version`, kick off the rebuild-benchmark-index
workflow) by hand.
- The skill won't author bug-fix PRs. Per `docs/developer.md` step 3.5,
fixes needed during the release window go in as separate PRs into dev
and the release branch is rebased; the skill flags this as an
anti-pattern (don't bundle fixes with release prep).

`CLAUDE.md`'s "Versioning and Changelog" section now points at the skill
from the same place that points at `version-bump`.

identified by the `desloppify` scan:

  `.github/actions/setup-r-env/action.yml` to encapsulate standard R
  environment setup. This eliminates significant boilerplate duplication

  test logic for different meter types.

  prevents 'input string 1 is invalid' errors when real secret keys are
  unavailable, ensuring test stability.

failure) were still Debug, making a dropped/skipped resume invisible
at default log level. Add logging.InfoThrottle (INFO-first,
Debug-repeat) and route those three sites through it, keyed per task
so a change in the skip reason re-arms INFO but a sustained cooldown

task in the exact same shape was falling through to the generic
stale-restart path and getting silently re-implemented instead of
resumed from its last completed run.

refactor(ONEK-267): migrate button hover colors to interactive tokens

* fix(ONEK-275): add missing fallback mappings for stages 6-10 and unit tests

Add 6 missing entries to mapRequestStatusToUIStatus() and
getWorkflowStepFromRequestStatus() so the fallback path
(when current_step is NULL) correctly resolves proposal_sent
through closed_won stages instead of defaulting to step 1.

Also fix hardcoded quotesTotal fallback from 5 to '?' in
FlightRequestCard to avoid misleading badge counts.

73 unit tests added covering both mapping utilities.

Closes ONEK-275, ONEK-276

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <<redacted>>

* fix(ui): migrate hardcoded colors to design system tokens across 27 files

Replace ~85 instances of hardcoded Tailwind color classes (blue-*, green-*,
red-*, orange-*, yellow-*, gray-*, slate-*) with semantic design system
tokens (primary, success, destructive, warning, info, muted, foreground,
background, border, etc.).

Key changes:
- P0: Chat components (UserMessage, ChatInterfaceRefactored, avinode-chat-thread)
- P1: Business components (quote-details-drawer, customer-selection-dialog,
  book-flight-modal, margin-edit-modal, quote-card, price-display, onboarding)
- P2: Gray neutrals (QuickActions, chat-loading-skeleton, conversation-starters)
- P3: Button outline/ghost hover states → sky-blue-50/primary, star ratings →
  warning token, design system page hex label corrections

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <<redacted>>

* docs(plans): add reverse-engineered feature decomposition with Obsidian wikilinks

Complete hierarchy: 15 Features → 35 Epics → 147 User Stories (Given/When/Then AC) → 265 Tasks
All files cross-linked with Obsidian [[wikilinks]] for graph navigation.
INDEX.md provides master navigation across all 462 plan items.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <<redacted>>

* docs: add ONEK Linear issue → feature decomposition mapping

Maps all 290 ONEK Linear issues to the plan hierarchy (15 Features,
35 Epics, 147 User Stories, 265 Tasks). Includes status tracking,
dependency chains, open work items, and unmapped plan items.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <<redacted>>

* feat(skills): add pr-followup-issues skill, replace one-time script

Convert the hardcoded PR #22 bash script into a reusable Claude Code
skill that analyzes any PR via gh CLI and generates categorized
follow-up Linear issues (CI, testing, performance, tech debt, docs,
security).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <<redacted>>

* fix(ONEK-290): repair email sending via Gmail MCP with connection recovery

The /api/email route was fetching a non-existent /api/mcp/gmail endpoint
instead of calling the email-service directly. The Gmail MCP client also
lacked connection recovery, so dropped stdio pipes caused permanent failures.

- Route now imports and calls sendEmail from email-service directly
- Gmail MCP client detects broken connections and retries once automatically
- Added resetConnection() to clean up stale singleton state on failure

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <<redacted>>

* fix(ONEK-289): show only client-facing prices on PDF proposals

FlightCard displayed the raw operator price (flight.totalPrice) while
PricingSection showed the marked-up total, confusing clients with two
different numbers. Now each flight's totalPrice is marked up with the
Jetvision fee before being passed to the PDF template.

- Added applyClientFacingPrices() to proposal-generator.ts
- Applied in both generateProposal() and prepareProposalData()
- Formula: basePrice × (1 + fee%) + taxes + fees per flight

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <<redacted>>

* refactor(commands): wire slash commands to auto-invoke matching skills

Replace inline workflow steps in 8 command files with Skill tool
invocation directives. Commands now load their SKILL.md via the Skill
tool instead of duplicating the workflow inline, ensuring a single
source of truth.

Commands updated: avinode-sandbox-test, cr

first_commit_message:
Add triage-trivy skill: structured CVE assessment for scan-containers failures (#790)

# Summary

Adds a `triage-trivy` skill at `.claude/skills/triage-trivy/SKILL.md`
for the agent to follow when the `scan-containers` CI job fails. Default
agent behavior on these failures has historically been "add to
`.trivyignore` and move on"; the skill is structured to make that the
harder path, requiring evidence-based per-CVE reasoning.

For each HIGH/CRITICAL CVE the agent: reads the CVE, identifies the
package's role in our containers, assesses whether the pipeline reaches
the vulnerable code path, searches for a fix (distro / base-image /
upstream conda — including an anaconda.org REST API recipe for the "fix
exists but the feedstock pins it out of reach" case), and decides
**Patch**, **Ignore**, or **Escalate**.

The Patch flow carries the design. The agent edits the affected
container yml (exact pin, one-line comment), commits, pushes, and opens
the PR with a rebuild-handoff callout at the top of the body — concrete
`bin/build_ecr_containers.py` invocation plus the git commit/push steps
for a user with ECR push to run. The PR opens with `scan-containers`
red; the user runs the rebuild, watches CI turn green, deletes the
callout from the body, and merges. The PR body is the persistent
rendezvous: agents that ran in a subagent session aren't reachable
later, so the handoff has to live somewhere the user can act on without
re-invoking.

**Anti-patterns the skill explicitly prevents:**

- Adding `.trivyignore` for a fixable CVE (this was previously the easy
escape on the rebuild gap; conflates "unfixable" with "out of this
environment's reach").
- "No Debian fix available" or "not exploited in production" as
standalone reasons.
- Vague expiry dates not tied to a re-evaluation trigger.
- Bulk-adding entries with one-line generic comments, or hiding the
assessment from the PR body.

**Dogfooded against this PR's own failing `scan-containers`**, which
surfaced urllib3 2.6.3 CVEs across five containers. Final disposition
under the skill: **Patch** on `multiqc` (transitive urllib3 via
`requests`, accepts an explicit `urllib3=2.7.0` pin); **Ignore** on the
four `awscli`-bearing containers (the awscli feedstock pins
`urllib3<=2.6.3` through every conda-forge build, so no reachable
rebuild ships the fix). That triage is on **PR #803**, stacked behind
this one.

`CLAUDE.md`'s "Checking CI Status" section points at this skill from any
Trivy CI failure, alongside the existing `ci-debugger` agent reference.

first_commit_message:
chore(skills): add build-install skill capturing the local rebuild + DMG-install flow

End-to-end macOS local install of ppxai: build all four PyInstaller
binaries (ppxai, ppxaide, ppxai-server, ppxai-desktop), VSCode
extension VSIX, and the macOS .app + DMG, then install everything to
the user's system locations the way an end-user install would.

The skill encodes the canonical sequence run on 2026-05-02 — first
PyInstaller build serial (initialises `build/` cache), remaining three
parallel, then VSIX build, then `create-macos-app.sh` for the .app +
DMG, then install. The DMG-install step mounts the DMG and copies
`ppxai.app` from the mounted volume rather than from `dist/ppxai.app`
directly, so it actually exercises the install path end users would
run.

`.gitignore` updated to track `.claude/skills/` alongside the existing
`.claude/commands/` exception so this and future skills live with the
repo.

Pre-existing edges captured:
* `npm install` only on first run / after a dep bump (the v1.18.2
  esbuild bundling switch surfaced the "Cannot find module 'esbuild'"
  failure mode).
* `code --install-extension --force` overwrites a previous install.
* `ppxai-desktop --version` is the v1.17.7 stale-version sentinel —
  flag if it reports the wrong string.

Invoke via the Skill tool with `skill: build-install` or by mentioning
"rebuild and reinstall" / "install from DMG".

resolved head, the reconciler's declared-surface containment). This
makes `DIRTY` a first-class pipeline task.

A new **`resolve`** task type joins scope/approve/implement/land in
`agent-work.yml`. `/land` dispatches it on `DIRTY` (`gh workflow run
agent-work.yml -f task=resolve -f ref=<pr>`) instead of
surfacing-and-stopping. `/resolve` (+ `/resolve-headless`) is an
`/implement`-shaped **pure producer**: it checks out the PR's branch,
merges `origin/main` into it (the merge-not-rebase mechanic from #3261),
resolves every conflict hunk — semantic ones included, no "too complex
to attempt" tier — commits the merge, non-force pushes, drives CI green
through the same Refine loop `/implement` uses, then re-requests the
review (`@barista review`) on the resolved head. It neither opens a PR
(the PR exists) nor merges (that is `/land`'s job); the resolved head
re-enters the reconciler → `phase:held` → land path. Self-bounce
(ask-and-park) fires only on a genuine incompatibility of intent — the
sole route to a person.

Depends on #3261 (merge-not-rebase), landed via #3266.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/agent-work.yml` — `resolve` task: dispatch enum
entry; `ref` description (PR number, like land);
`8cpu-linux-x64/extras=s3-cache` runner + 90-min leash folded in with
implement (resolve runs the same CI Refine loop); re-entrancy-guard
`resolve)` arm (`proceed=false` on a merged PR or a `mergeable_state`
that is neither `dirty` nor `unknown`); closing-issue model resolution
(`land|resolve`); 400 max-turns.
- `.github/workflows/agent-chat.yml`,
`.claude/skills/headless/protocol.md` — **fallout the scope caught**:
register `resolve` in the parked-answer whitelist (`case "$task"`) and
the park-marker grammar so a resolve park's owner reply re-dispatches.
- `.claude/skills/resolve/**`, `.claude/skills/resolve-headless/**` —
the new resolve-box skill and its headless wrapper, modeled on
`/implement` + `/implement-headless`.
- `.claude/skills/land/SKILL.md` — `DIRTY` dispatches `resolve` and
aborts; `--sweep` dispatch-and-continue (no longer halts); the
behind-merge and oracle-disagreement dirty paths route the same way;
"What /land does NOT do" first bullet updated.
- `.claude/skills/land-headless/SKILL.md` — drop the dirty-conflict
ask-and-park override row (dirty is no longer a human touchpoint);
description adjusted.

## Test plan

CI yaml-lint on the two workflows; the workflows' own convention makes
the first live `resolve` dispatch the acceptance test. The skill prose
is reviewed for consistency against `/implement` and `/land`.

## Beyond the declared surface

- `.gitignore` — the `.claude/skills/` directory is
gitignore-allowlisted (`.claude/skills/*` + per-skill `!` un-ignore
entries), so the declared `.claude/skills/resolve/**` files cannot be
tracked without adding `!.claude/skills/resolve/` and
`!.claude/skills/resolve-headless/`. A mechanical necessity to realize
the plan's explicit declared files; the scope's declared surface missed
the allowlist mechanic. Two lines, surfaced here transparently — the
same class as the agent-chat.yml / protocol.md fallout the scope itself
recorded.

* wip: auto-commit uncommitted agent work

Signed-off-by: sybra-app[bot] <<redacted>>

* fix(workflow): promote resume-stalled skips to throttled INFO

ResumeStalled's skip-reason logs (retry_after, status skip, claim
failure) were still Debug, making a dropped/skipped resume invisible
at default log level. Add logging.InfoThrottle (INFO-first,
Debug-repeat) and route those three sites through it, keyed per task
so a change in the skip reason re-arms INFO but a sustained cooldown
doesn't flood the log.

Also generalize Recovery.recoverCompletedHeadlessRun beyond
review-tagged tasks: its existing guards (headless mode, stopped
state, definitive outcome, non-terminal workflow, unrecorded current
step, no running agent) were already tag-agnostic, so a non-review
task in the exact same shape was falling through to the generic

grep inside $(...) command substitutions under `set -euo pipefail`.

through the substitution and terminating the hook before the

no-match return empty string rather than aborting the hook.

any bare npm publish survives stripping, the hook fires as expected.

Guard release coherence mechanically, at the two moments it can break (issue #308) (#311)

* Guard release coherence mechanically, at the two moments it can break (issue #308)

Issue #308 was found by a human reading main. Both defects it surfaced are
mechanical, and neither failed a test, broke a build, or showed up in a diff.

PR-time (ci.yml, a new 'changelog' job): every v* tag must have its own
'## [x.y.z]' section. This is the check that fails the PR which erased v0.43.0
and v0.47.0 — a bump that renames the *previous* release's header instead of
adding its own. The diff of such a PR looks like an ordinary new section; only
the whole file, read against the tag list, shows a published version has gone
missing. fetch-depth: 0 is load-bearing — the shallow default fetches no tags,
and the check refuses to pass on an empty tag list rather than read green
forever on an input it cannot find.

Tag-time (release.yml, a new 'preflight' job gating build): the tag must match
_version.py, that version must have a section, and [Unreleased] must be empty.
The first because hatchling reads the version from the code, not the tag — so a
v0.72.0 tag on a commit still saying 0.71.0 publishes a 0.71.0 wheel, silently.
The last because [Unreleased] is a legal staging area right up until a release
claims otherwise: that is issue #308's exact state, and it now cannot ship.
Nothing is built or published until this passes.

The ordering is total by construction. A bare int() over version parts raised
ValueError on 'v1.0.0rc1' — a legal PEP 440 tag that release.yml fires on — and
because a tag does not go away, that would have crashed the changelog job on
every later PR too, bricking CI with the check meant to protect it. A guard that
dies on an input it did not anticipate is worse than the bug it catches.

Also corrects a stale comment in release.yml: the pypi env-gate is actuated by
the capital via its operator credential, not by the founder, who is out of the
publish loop (constitution.md -> Earned Autonomy).

* Document the preflight gate in the release skill

CLAUDE.md -> Releasing points at this skill for the full pipeline, so a release
that now fails at a new first step needs its remedy documented here: fix main,
delete and re-push the tag — never force it. Also states the captain's build
duty precisely: promote [Unreleased] into the version's own section, and never
fold a change into an already-dated one.

fix(start): scrub stale git extraheader before boot pull (#278)

* fix(start): scrub stale git extraheader before boot pull

A past manual `git push` workaround can bake a point-in-time
`http.<host>.extraheader` Basic token into the kube-coder clone's
.git/config. Git sends an extraheader verbatim, so once the hourly
GitHub App token rotates the baked value goes stale and shadows the
self-refreshing global credential.helper, silently breaking every git
op on the clone — including start.sh's own boot `git pull --ff-only`,
which then hits its "skipped" branch and leaves the source stale
indefinitely.

Strip any stale extraheader (idempotent) before the boot pull so the
dynamic credential.helper is always used.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <<redacted>>

* docs(skills): git push works; add extraheader-scrub regression test

Now that the stale-extraheader footgun is scrubbed at boot, plain
`git push` works via the self-refreshing global credential.helper, so
the kc-ship-pr skill's "git push does not work, use the Git Data API"
premise is obsolete. Rewrite it to push normally, keep the Git Data API
as a documented fallback, and point at the extraheader unset as the
first thing to try when a push is wedged.

Also add a helm-unittest assertion that start.sh scrubs the stale
extraheader before the boot pull, so the fix can't silently regress.
